Re: Return of security deposit – [flat address]

Dear Mr/Ms [Name],

I vacated the flat at [address] on [date] and returned the keys to you / [person] on [date]. The security deposit of CHF 4,500 was paid under our tenancy agreement dated [date].

I understand you intend to retain the deposit on the basis that the walls require repainting. I do not accept that the flat was damaged beyond normal wear and tear. At the time of move-out, the walls were in normal condition consistent with six years of ordinary use, apart from minor furniture marks, which I consider normal use/wear and not damage for which I should be liable.

Under Swiss tenancy law, a landlord may retain only amounts that are actually due and must provide a detailed, itemized statement for any deductions. Normal wear and tear, minor scuffs, and ordinary aging of paint are not the tenant's responsibility. A full repainting of the flat would not be a reasonable or necessary remedy for minor furniture marks unless the lease/inventory specifically shows that the walls were in a different condition at move-in or that I caused damage.

Therefore, please provide within 14 days of the date of this letter:
1. an itemized statement of the amounts you propose to deduct, with calculations;
2. the signed move-in and move-out inventories, if any;
3. dated photographs of the alleged wall damage showing the rooms and areas;
4. the repair invoice(s) or written professional quote(s), including scope, walls to be painted, colours, labour and material costs, and the basis for concluding a full repaint is necessary rather than local touch-up/repair;
5. confirmation of the amount to be returned by bank transfer to [IBAN] and the expected date.

I am willing to discuss reasonable and documented costs for damage actually caused beyond normal use. However, I ask that the deposit be released promptly once a fair, substantiated deduction, if any, has been agreed or determined.

If I do not receive the requested documentation and a final statement by [date], I will consider the matter unresolved and may seek assistance from a tenant advice organization / mediation / the competent tenancy arbitration/court to recover the deposit.

Please confirm receipt of this letter and your response by [date].

Yours sincerely,
[Name]
[Signature]

[Your name]

[Email]

[Landlord/Property management]
[Address]

Re: Security deposit – [flat address]; tenancy ended [date]

Dear [Name],

I am writing regarding the security deposit of CHF 4,500.00 for the flat at [address]. I vacated the flat on [date] and returned the keys on [date].

I understand that you have stated that the walls are scuffed and require repainting, and that you intend to retain the deposit. I do not agree that I am liable for the full amount. At the time of handover, the flat was in normal condition after six years of ordinary use. Minor furniture marks are normal wear and tear, not damage beyond ordinary use. A full repainting of the flat would be disproportionate unless you can show specific damage that goes beyond normal wear and that the walls were in a different condition when I moved in.

Please provide, within 14 days of receipt of this letter:
1. a detailed itemized statement of all amounts you intend to deduct from the deposit, with calculations;
2. the move-in and move-out inventories/handover protocols, if any;
3. dated photos of the alleged damage, showing the affected rooms and areas;
4. the repair invoice(s) or written quote(s) from a professional, including the exact scope (which walls, whether touch-up or full repaint, colours, labour and material costs) and the basis for the cost;
5. confirmation of the net amount to be returned and the date you will transfer it to [IBAN].

I am prepared to discuss a reasonable, documented charge for actual damage beyond normal wear. However, I ask that you not retain the deposit without a proper, itemized justification.

If I do not receive the requested documentation and a final statement by [date], I will treat the deposit as outstanding and may seek assistance from a tenant advice organization, mediation, or the competent tenancy arbitration/court to recover the amount.

Please confirm receipt of this letter by email or post.

Yours sincerely,
[Signature]
[Name]
